title: Ìomhar Dearg comes to the ford
summary: Ìomhar Dearg, a son of Ailean Mòr, who had stayed three days in the valley under Dùn ìseal arguing for river-grazing, comes down out of the heather to Àth na Fala on the morning after the king fell, and finds the river dammed by the dead and his father on the west bank.

title: The spent host broken at the ford
summary: Ìomhar Dearg's household crosses the ford and falls on the host of the east where it lies spent in the heather. Many are killed, many run, and some sit down and cover their heads. By evening Ìomhar holds the ford.

title: The greybeard found in the ford
summary: The greybeard of the eastern households who gave the counsel of the third day is found at dawn face down in the shallows below the king's stone. Whether he fell or went in of his own will, nobody on the east bank will say.

title: Dùn dhearg taken and its halls burned
summary: Ìomhar Dearg walks in through both gates of Dùn dhearg, where the households of the east had sworn they owed nothing to Dùn ìseal. No one will own the blow that felled the king. He has the halls within the double bank burned, and takes the people under his own hand.

title: The bier of spears
summary: On the fifth day after the ford the king's body is laid on a bier lashed from the host's spears and carried up the valley road by twelve men of Dùn dhearg who had been in the river. Two grey sons of the king meet it at the lip of the valley and walk behind it. Ìomhar Dearg does not go with it.

title: The dead of the ford buried on the meadow
summary: Ìomhar Dearg has the dead of the host drawn out of the river and buried in long trenches on the meadow, all together, since none can be told apart. The king's stone at the head of the ford is left standing, and he forbids anyone to move it.

title: The twelve bearers given cattle
summary: The twelve bearers come back to Dùn dhearg with the poles of the bier. Ìomhar Dearg gives each a cow and a place within the bank, and sets the poles up at the inner gate.
